note: The field of the place picture beyond the frame, as shares of the frame's width and height: left, right, bottom, top. Measured on the place picture itself (diag view beauty/picture at frames 2448 and 2706): the relief's apron is painted to the left and below as far as an eighth of the frame, to the right its outer layers end between 0.066 and 0.08 of the width beyond the frame, the sky above has no end.
pathNote: The sidestep of the dive, in radii in the frame of the camera that leaves the hold (right, up), complete by the given share of the way to T. Phobos hangs 0.66 radii in front of the hold camera and 0.1 radii off its axis, low and to the right. The steady descent alone passed 0.012 radii from its surface in frame 2406 and the moon filled a third of that one frame. A sidestep to the left showed the flank of the moon, where its picture is stretched. With this one the camera lifts over the moon, as the frozen build did: the moon leaves by the bottom edge over frames 2400 to 2404, seen from above, and the camera passes 0.18 radii from its centre.
riseNote: The rise leaves from the eye of the dive (path.fromDive, the power of the lead). The plates of the globe are laid back from the twin of the dive (height 0.0017193 radii, pitch -17.75 degrees), and a lay back is true from that one eye only. The rise first had a twin of its own, 0.0023 radii ahead of that eye and 0.001 below it, 1.47 twin heights away: the picture of one eye over plates of another showed as stripes of the globe through the cliff (frames 2692 to 2697) and as a patch with straight sides (2698 to 2711). Now the close path of the rise is led from frame 2670 to the pose the dive handed over at and T is frame 2692 (at 0.2973): 22 frames of pulling back and up, then 52 frames of glide where the dive has 54, so the rise is the dive in reverse, frame f at the height of dive frame 5144 minus f. With T at 2698 (at 0.3734) the glide had 46 frames and the body colour stepped by 8.32 into frame 2737, over the limit of 8; with 2692 the largest step is 6.43 into 2736. The window is 12 frames as in the dive. No limit on enlargement is set on either side: tried with 1.2 on frames 2446 and 2698, the far wall of the picture turned hazy and the strokes on its left half stayed.
edgeNote: edgeIn: left, right, bottom, top, as shares of the frame. While the picture's weight is under 1 its sides feather inward by this share times what is missing of the weight, so the picture comes in from the place outward and leaves toward it. Without it the right side of the picture stood as a straight slanted line against lighter ground in frames 2446 to 2449 and a pale wedge with a straight side at the upper right in 2444 to 2446. The top is less because the far field carries the horizon. Judged on every frame 2436 to 2459 and 2670 to 2744 at the draft tier: body colour steps into 2443 to 2454 between 0.92 and 3.45 (1.09 and 3.13 without).
limbNote: The close view has a bright band of dust haze on its horizon that the globe side does not draw. In the place window the camera is above the twin, so its limb lies beyond the horizon of the picture (8 pixels at frame 2447): the globe's dark sky and stars showed in that gap as a dark line under the haze. With limbReachDeg the sky of the picture is pushed down onto the limb of the camera, less and less up to that many degrees above it, and the ground the twin could not see takes the horizon row of the picture. At T nothing moves. Measured on frames 2444 to 2453 of the dive; the rise has the same eye.
